I added `from __future__ import annotations` to all 20 carrier modules in `shop/carriers/`. `__init__.py` is unchanged, and nothing else in the files changed (20 one-line insertions).

In each file the new line is the first import, sitting just above `import re`, so it comes after the TODO comment and the module docstring. It can't go any higher: if it came before the docstring, Python would no longer treat the docstring as the module's docstring.

**Tests:** `pytest` isn't installed, so I ran the suite with `python3 -m unittest discover`, and all 6 tests passed. Those tests cover cache, orders and pricing, though, not the carriers. As a separate check I imported `shop.carriers`, which loads all 20 modules, and it worked without errors.
